entries.clue: What a Briton puts the kettle on for
Tall metal vessel with a tap, keeping a church hall in hot water
Planted collection of trees grown for study and display, as at Westonbirt
Lumps or spoonfuls of sweetness, offered round before the stir
Crotchety eldest inhabitant, handy with his stick, doting on a far younger wife
Tree cut back high, out of reach of grazing cattle and deer
Garden tree hung with yellow chains in May, its pea-like pods deadly
Axe-like tool with its blade set crosswise, swung to shape a beam
Pirate captain resigned to scuttling his own ship when familiar sails appear
Draped garment the heroes borrow when sneaking around the enemy capital
Carved monolith the strongman sculpts, sells and delivers slung on his back
Malty Indian state whose black harvest anchors breakfast blends
